name: Optuna (RDBStorage)
param_style: SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM session.query compiled by the sqlite dialect; ? positional; selectinload expands IN lists in batches of 500
schema_source: optuna/storages/_rdb/models.py: tables created by RDBStorage itself (metadata.create_all, optuna 5.0.0 from PyPI) on SQLite and dumped with .schema; alembic head v3.2.0.a
data_scale: scale 1: 6 studies, 34k trials (20k in the LightGBM study, 8k NSGA-II 2-objective, 5.1k XGBoost CV, 3 x 300), 191k params, 30k values, 460k intermediate values, 43k system attrs, 37k user attrs; 62 MB
visibility_note: 15k stars; the most-used Python hyperparameter optimisation framework; sqlite:/// is the documented default for persistent studies and optuna-dashboard
interest_note: TPE and every sampler re-read the study through _CachedStorage: a full-study load is one ordered trial scan plus five selectinload IN(500) batches per 500 trials; best_trial sorts all complete trials on a CASE key no index can serve; count_past_trials makes trial creation O(n).
reach_note: developer tool; SQLite file storage is the default persistent backend for local studies and optuna-dashboard

cpu_evidence.summary: 1000-trial, 2-param study: 1m42s with SQLite storage vs 6.9s in memory; the per-trial storage round trips (trial loads, count_past_trials) dominate
mysqldumpslow on a sample study flags the best_trial query (join + ORDER BY CASE over value_type) as the slowest statement
bottleneck with 100+ concurrent sessions until trials.study_id got an index (present at the pinned SHA as ix_trials_study_id)
SQLite 'too many SQL variables' from the IN list of unfinished trial ids in the incremental _get_trials; the code now falls back to a full study read
